anf_compare.notes: ANF has no text of this homily; translated directly from the PG 93 Greek.

choices.why: Hortatory aorist subjunctive, the first of the section's exhortations.

choices.term: ἃς ἡμεῖς ἐλλαμφθῆναι ταῖς ἡμετέραις διανοίαις εὐξώμεθα
choices.english: let us pray that these may shine into our minds
rejected: which we wish to be illuminated by in our minds
choices.why: The rays are the subject of the passive infinitive: they are to shine into our minds.
ἅλμη is sea-brine; 'bitter' spells out its taste within the sea image and adds no claim.

choices.english: as we travel the restless sea
choices.why: ἄστατος describes the sea, not the travellers.

choices.term: τὸν κλύδωνα τῶν ψυχοφθόρων κυμάτων ἐκφύγωμεν
choices.english: escape the surge of the soul-destroying waves
rejected: flee the sea of the surge
choices.why: κλύδων is the surge itself, the object of ἐκφύγωμεν.

pass_a_gloss: [completing the previous section: '…but above the'] heavens it is; they have the light unquenchable, the course unceasing, the rays ever-shining, which [rays] let us pray (εὔχομαι) to be shone into (ἐλλάμπω) our minds. And let us escape the darkness itself, and let us turn aside from the brine (ἅλμη) of life, and, travelling the unstable (ἄστατος) sea, let us escape the surge (κλύδων) of the soul-destroying waves, and [the sentence continues in the next section].
pass_b_english: …heavens. They have a light that cannot be quenched, a course that never ceases, rays that always shine; let us pray that these may shine into our minds. Let us flee the darkness itself, turn aside from the bitter brine of life, and, as we travel the restless sea, escape the surge of the soul-destroying waves, and…
source_text:
οὐρανῶν ἐστιν, τὸ φῶς ἔχουσιν ἄσβεστον, τὸν δρόμον ἀκατάπαυστον, τὰς ἀκτῖνας
ἀειφανεῖς, ἃς ἡμεῖς ἐλλαμφθῆναι ταῖς ἡμετέραις διανοίαις εὐξώμεθα. Καὶ αὐτὸ τὸ
σκότος ἐκφύγωμεν καὶ τοῦ βίου τὴν ἅλμην ἐκκλίνωμεν καὶ τὴν ἄστατον
πορευόμενοι θάλασσαν τὸν κλύδωνα τῶν ψυχοφθόρων κυμάτων ἐκφύγωμεν καὶ
